document.title: Strategy for Eliminating the Threat from the Jihadist Networks of al-Qida: Status and Prospects (Tab A)
document.authors: NSC Counterterrorism Security Group staff (Richard Clarke)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Bush Administration's First Memo on al-Qaeda Declassified
document.note: December 2000 Clinton-era NSC strategy paper, attached to the Clarke memo as Tab A. It reviews the al-Qaeda threat and the record to date, incorporates the CIA's Blue Sky ideas, and poses near-term policy choices. The goal was to roll back al-Qaeda over three to five years. It warns that continued operations at the current level 'will not seriously attrite their ability to plan and conduct attacks'.

events.description: Al Qida moved its headquarters from Sudan to Afghanistan after diplomatic pressure on Sudan.
Usama bin Ladin publicly declared war on the United States.
Al Qida suicide truck-bombed US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania.
US struck al Qida facilities in Afghanistan and an associated chemical plant in Sudan.
Simultaneous disruption of over twenty al Qida cells to prevent Millennium attacks.
CIA began covert Predator UAV flights into Afghanistan from Uzbekistan.
Successful attack on a US Navy ship in Yemen.
US and Russia co-sponsored further UN sanctions on Taliban (arms embargo); passed 13-0-2.
Attack on USS Cole, after which Pakistan asked the US not to violate its airspace for punitive strikes.
Pakistan rendered Khalil Deek to Jordan, criticized by Islamic parties.
Proposed resumption of Predator UAV operations.
CIA created a 'Virtual Station' dedicated to collection against al Qida.
Saudis disrupted a plot by an al Qida cell in the Kingdom; CIA identifying cells and working with local services.
Near-simultaneous suicide truck bombings destroyed the US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania.
US struck al Qida facilities in Afghanistan and a chemical plant in Sudan.
US began telling Taliban leadership they were culpable for harboring al Qida.
UN sanctions on Afghanistan sponsored by Saudis and US; US seized over $250,000,000 in Taliban funds.
US and Russia co-sponsored further UN sanctions; passed 13-0-2 with China and Malaysia abstaining.
Al Qida moved its headquarters from Sudan to Afghanistan after US diplomatic pressure on Sudan.
Attempted attack on US Air Force personnel in Yemen in which al Qida played a role.
World Trade Center bombing and Mogadishu attack on US forces, with indications of al Qida role.
Al Qida attacked US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania.
Planned multi-site attacks on Americans in Jordan, disrupted; al Qida cell involved.
Successful attack on a US Navy ship in Yemen following earlier failed attempt.
CIA created a 'Virtual Station' focused on al Qida.
CIA proposal: massive support to anti-Taliban groups such as the Northern Alliance.
Proposed continuation of Predator UAV operations, resuming in March.
Possible introduction of armed UAVs into Afghanistan in the Spring if testing succeeds.
Pakistan rendered Khalil Deek to Jordan.
After the attack on the USS Cole, Pakistan asked the US not to violate Pakistani airspace for punitive strikes in Afghanistan.

key_claims: Al Qida is both an independent terrorist organization and sponsor/coordinator of semi-independent terrorist groups.
Al Qida moved its HQ to Afghanistan in 1996 and trained up to 50,000 jihadists in Afghan camps.
Mullah Omar has blocked any Taliban action against al Qida despite some willing Taliban leaders.
Al Qida provides the Taliban's best fighting unit (55th Brigade) and buys provincial leaders' support.
Pakistani Army provides advisors and training to the Taliban; Pakistan's support flows from the strategic depth concept and Kashmir.
The strategy proposes covert aid to Masood's Northern Alliance and continued armed Predator operations.
Al-Qida's center of gravity is its sanctuary in Afghanistan under Taliban sponsorship.
Pakistan's support for the Taliban across the Bhutto, Sharif and Musharraf governments rests on 'strategic depth' against India.
Pakistan's tolerance of Taliban-hosted terrorist camps and bin Laden stems from the nexus with its proxy war in Kashmir.
Pakistan cooperates on terrorism mainly when its role is invisible or deniable to Islamist parties.
Overt Pakistani support for US action against bin Laden would threaten Musharraf's government.
US levers on Pakistan include UNSC sanctions, domestic opposition to Sunni extremists, and IMF economic support.
Musharraf says Pakistan cannot or will not persuade the Taliban to yield bin Ladin.
